claim: MAIN RESULT. The ideal generated by the six matching generators, saturated at q(q-1) != 0 by the Rabinowitsch variable u with u*q*(q-1) - 1 = 0, is ZERO-DIMENSIONAL of DEGREE EXACTLY 2 over K = Q(i*sqrt(11)), the field in which the matching equations' own coefficients live via s+ = -1/6 + i*sqrt(11)/6 and delta = -i*sqrt(11)/3. Computed as the number of standard monomials under a grevlex Groebner basis over an exact algebraic number field, so the result is exact, not numerical. The lex eliminant in theta_inf is theta_inf^2 + 4*theta_inf + 107/27, proportional to 27*theta_inf^2 + 108*theta_inf + 107, which is EXACTLY the polynomial registered as a prediction in PREREG.md section 4 BEFORE the computation was run; its roots are -2 - sqrt(3)/9 and -2 + sqrt(3)/9. The two solutions are therefore GALOIS CONJUGATE over K under sqrt(3) -> -sqrt(3), which is the same symmetry that relates the two branches in S22-20. Recorded finding from arm V4: the unsaturated ideal also has degree 2, so for this particular ideal the saturation removed nothing, meaning there is no spurious component on q = 0 or q = 1 introduced by clearing denominators. That the saturation machinery is nonetheless active is established separately by row G of the known-answer battery (S25-05).
label: PROVEN

claim: The no-apparent-singularity condition b1 = 0 lies in the RADICAL of the ideal generated by the five coefficient-matching equations together with the Rabinowitsch generator. Decided exactly: b1 reduces to 0 modulo the grevlex Groebner basis of that ideal, so it lies in the ideal itself and a fortiori in the radical; independently, adjoining 1 - v*b1 yields the UNIT ideal [1]. The membership test carries its own control: theta_inf, which vanishes nowhere on the variety since the eliminant's roots are -2 +/- sqrt(3)/9, is correctly reported as NOT in the radical, so the test is not accepting everything. MATHEMATICAL CONTENT, stated in its own right rather than only as the explanation of a failed arm: matching the two quartics ALREADY FORCES b1 = 0. The no-apparent-singularity condition did not need to be imposed as a separate requirement, and CT-S16's system is overdetermined to that extent.
label: PROVEN

claim: TWO PRE-REGISTERED SENSITIVITY ARMS WITHDRAWN AS ILL-POSED, both left unedited in place with their outputs retained, per the handling used for CT-S22 Stage 5A. V3, from PREREG.md section 5, required the degree to move when b1 = 0 was dropped and fired when it did not; its stated inference, that a weaker generating set must define a larger variety, is invalid whenever the dropped polynomial lies in the radical of the others, which S25-03 proves is the case here. V3b, from PREREG-ADDENDUM.md, was written specifically to discriminate redundancy from insensitivity by dropping each coefficient equation in turn and requiring movement for at least one; it moved for none and so declared the instrument void. Its inference is invalid for the same reason: the system is six generators in four unknowns cutting out two points, overdetermined by two, so no single generator need be load bearing and a null response is uninterpretable. TRANSFERABLE FINDING: this is the second arm in one session to fail in the class of S23-07, the second having been authored with the first explicitly in mind. The diagnosis is that SENSITIVITY IS THE WRONG INSTRUMENT TEST FOR AN OVERDETERMINED SYSTEM, because redundancy absorbs any single perturbation. The correct instrument test is a KNOWN-ANSWER CONTROL, which does not touch the target system at all. Recorded rather than repaired by a third sensitivity arm, which would have been the start of a regress ending wherever the desired answer appeared.
label: STRUCTURAL

claim: KNOWN-ANSWER CONTROL for the degree-counting code path, replacing the withdrawn sensitivity arms and following the CT-S22 Stage 1 pattern. Seven ideals of independently known degree were run through the IDENTICAL code path, in the same ring, over the same field K = Q(i*sqrt(11)), in the same variables, with the same Rabinowitsch generator; all expected values were fixed in PREREG-ADDENDUM-2.md section 3 before the battery was run. The pre-declared falsifier was that any row returning other than its stated value would render every degree in the session VOID, including the main degree-2 result.

claim: N1 CLOSES. The solution set of the CT-S16 matching system, saturated at q(q-1) != 0, is EXACTLY the two points recorded in CT-S16-MEMBERSHIP-C/outputs/pq_solution.txt, so the phrase 'for both sign branches' in S16-12 is EXHAUSTIVE and no longer rests on sp.solve. Established by two independent routes. Counting route: the degree is 2, bounding the number of points over the algebraic closure counted with multiplicity by 2, while V1 exhibits two DISTINCT points in the variety, so each has multiplicity 1. Constructive route: the lex Groebner basis in order u > p > q > t > theta_inf is TRIANGULAR, with u, p, q and t each appearing to degree exactly 1 in a basis element whose only other variable is theta_inf, so each root of the eliminant determines at most one point; the eliminant has exactly two distinct roots -2 +/- sqrt(3)/9; and back-substituting each root returns exactly one point in (p, q, t, u), which matches the corresponding CT-S16 recorded solution exactly. SCOPE: this settles only whether sp.solve's two solutions were all of them. It says nothing about the derivation that produced the six generators, which is CT-S16's and is unchanged here.
label: PROVEN
